concern: Reframe 240/240 and remove perfect-score headlines; explain trial variation.
response: We agree. This is exact error-set agreement for eight specified regression checks, not real-world detection accuracy. Seeds 1–30 vary the generated Association topology; mutation fixtures and rules remain fixed.
action: Abstract, Introduction, fault methodology/results, conclusion, and fault-code table revised. The evaluator now fails on any non-exact error set; legacy metric columns remain for compatibility.

concern: State impact-set sizes and explain the oracle result.
response: The original undirected sets cover 94/100, 979/1,000, 9,781/10,000 and 49,045/50,000 synthetic IDs, and 48–49 IDs in the 65-object case. Oracle equality checks connected-component implementation.
action: Abstract, Results, Discussion and Conclusion now state this boundary. New typed/bounded/change-aware policies are evaluated separately; no business-impact accuracy is claimed.

concern: Reconcile the report complexity explanation with observed ratios and validation exponents.
response: The repeated-scan bound describes one code component, not a fitted growth law. Report ratios of about 225 and 43 exceed the simple 100 and 25 factors; allocation/cache/runtime effects were not instrumented and cannot be attributed. Validation ratios 14.3 and 4.4 do not establish one exponent.
action: Results retains those historical measurements, qualifies the explanation, implements one-pass report counts, and adds separately labeled local revision measurements.

concern: Correct the number of semantically valid scenarios.
response: Seven scenarios have no expected errors; CR04, CR07 and CR08 contain the specified findings.
action: Corrected “Eight” to “Seven” in the controlled-change results.

concern: Disclose single-type application-heavy scale models and fixed impact seed.
response: The scale-growing graph uses ApplicationComponent/Association with two fixed Assignment/Serving fixtures; app.000000 is the impact seed. This is not a balanced enterprise model.
action: Synthetic-model methodology and threats state the vocabulary, topology artifact and seed explicitly.

concern: Use consistent statistics, mark the hardware break, emphasize n=3, and temper governance claims.
response: All original scaling figures now show medians or maximum RSS, without normal-approximation confidence bands. Intel-to-AMD breaks are marked; report/portal n=3 is explicit. Organizational governance was not evaluated.
action: Title/abstract repositioned toward EA repository validation. Rebuilt figures from recovered raw CSVs; captions state axis scales and sample sizes.

concern: Reframe RQ4; trim unused connector formalism; map faults to codes; define quality score; fix units and references.
response: Reproducibility is now a statement. The unused connector set was removed. The quality score is defined as a heuristic and excluded from empirical outcomes. The Kubernetes reference now uses pp. 1–7; the submitted MDDOAI spelling was already consistent and is retained.
action: Formalism simplified, fault-code table added, quality formula defined, 627 ms typography fixed, and figure scales stated.

concern: Archive the evaluated commits with a DOI and publish workflow run IDs.
response: The exact commits, original run IDs, recovered CSV/environment artifacts and timeout log are now preserved. A permanent archival deposit has not been completed: a GitHub branch or metadata file is not an archival DOI.
action: Open Science section and provenance manifest identify framework run 35993083302 / commit d3ba12e3105b9edbe294d98059e611ccefb8820b and companion run 35990375878 / commit 59fe34511b830f5181e7782d6b9d3fbaf78d9227. Archival metadata/checklist prepared. The author must complete the deposit and insert the issued DOI.

concern: Reframe the perfect-score result.
response: Agreed. Catalog conformance and repeated topology variants cannot estimate accuracy on arbitrary real EA defects.
action: Removed precision/recall/F1 headlines throughout; exact-match regression framing and check-to-code mapping used instead.

concern: Implement a report index and re-attempt 100,000 objects.
response: The renderer now counts Serving and Access relationships in one pass. Default report output is byte-identical on Metroville. A separate local protocol repeats all stages at sizes through 100,000; it is explicitly distinct from the original hosted 30-repetition experiment.
action: Indexed report and adjacency traversal implemented, validated, and measured. Raw revision CSVs, stage progress, resource telemetry and environment are supplied.

concern: Make the integration contribution visible against existing AaC and EA tooling.
response: The revision acknowledges prior continuous EA pipelines, Git-based Archi collaboration, Structurizr validation/publication, and LeanIX target planning. No unique-invention or cross-tool performance superiority claim is made.
action: Added a primary-source capability table and EA maintenance literature; positioned the contribution as this open integration and auditable characterization.

concern: Address broad impact sets and the unsupported scale ceiling.
response: Legacy component sizes remain reported. Typed and change-aware policies now give distinct candidate sets under explicit heuristics. The historical timeout remains an implementation/protocol limitation; the new local completion cannot be generalized into a production ceiling.
action: Added policy table, independent fixed-point checks, before/after snapshot scopes, and separately labeled revision performance results.

concern: Discuss practical use in real organizations.
response: A bounded adoption path is outlined: a scoped inventory, stable IDs, accountable owners, explicit mapping, and reviewed updates. This is an adoption proposal; no production deployment or organizational benefit is asserted.
action: Practical Implications and integration discussion revised; external-validity limitations and practitioner protocol supplied.

concern: Clarify undirected impact limitations.
response: Undirected reachability returns components and cannot distinguish business consequences. New dependency and depth-bound semantics are review heuristics with explicit exclusions.
action: Design, results and threats revised; policy documentation and per-ID explanations added.

concern: Discuss report-generation optimization.
response: Repeated per-row full-edge scans were removed. Sorting and the underlying validator/rules still contribute to total report cost.
action: Single-pass aggregate counters implemented, report equivalence verified, and supplemental measurements supplied.

concern: Explain coexistence with established EA tools.
response: Stable IDs, explicit source ownership and model/property/view mappings are prerequisites. Exchange formats and vendor APIs offer integration points, but a lossless adapter and synchronization connector have not been implemented or evaluated.
action: Integration section states the proposed route and current limits without implying working vendor connectivity.

concern: Identify the EA body-of-knowledge contribution and use EA maintenance literature.
response: The contribution is continuous EA repository and model-quality management. It is not a new EA language, complete governance method, or the first use of continuous delivery for EA.
action: Title, abstract, introduction, related work, discussion and conclusion revised; Farwick et al. and Sabau/Hacks/Steffens added from publisher records.

concern: Distinguish data-quality rules from architecture-board governance.
response: PR review can carry compliance evidence and an exception request, but boards still own approval, dispensation authority and contracts. Those organizational responsibilities are neither implemented nor evaluated.
action: Explicit governance boundary and TOGAF mapping added. Claims narrowed to machine-side repository checks.

concern: Demonstrate baseline, target, transition and gap analysis.
response: The new companion demonstration materializes three repositories with stable IDs, explicit Plateau/Gap concepts and a replacement platform. It validates each state and asserts an inventory diff, not target-architecture compliance or business approval.
action: Added diff CLI and snapshot-aware impact, run_roadmap.py, all three state snapshots, and gap-analysis.json. Baseline-to-target: one added object, three modified objects, one added and one removed relationship.

concern: Implement directed, relationship-type-aware impact for architecture decisions.
response: Serving/Realization/Assignment/Triggering/Flow, part-to-whole containment, and read/write Access propagation are explicitly specified. Association and intent links are excluded. These directions require organizational review and do not prove decision usefulness.
action: Implemented dependency policy, raw direction/type filters, depth bounds, predecessor explanations and before/after scope; added hand-written unit fixtures and independent scenario oracles.

concern: Use a realistic cross-layer repository and clarify synthetic scope.
response: Metroville already contains cross-layer business, application, technology, motivation and migration concepts, but is fictional and small. New architecture-state evidence exercises a cross-layer platform change. No real/anonymized organizational model or verified exchange adapter is supplied.
action: Original synthetic scope made explicit and fictional-case limits retained. Cross-layer inventory-gap demonstration added.

concern: Add a practitioner evaluation and establish stakeholder value.
response: No practitioners have been recruited and no usability, effort or governance-value measurements exist. Simulated responses would not address this concern. The manuscript now disclaims those outcomes.
action: Prepared a task/counterbalancing protocol and empty observation template. Genuine sessions and an updated analysis are needed if the authors pursue stakeholder-value claims.

concern: Clarify what EA-Ops enables compared with existing tools.
response: It provides a particular inspectable combination of YAML facts, explicit constraints, Git review and generated evidence. We do not claim a new architect decision unavailable in other tools, nor replacement of broader commercial EA capabilities.
action: Capability comparison and contribution-boundary paragraphs added; priority and uniqueness language removed.

concern: Fix timing precision, enlarge Figure 2, condense perfect-score table, state derivation scope, and deposit DOI.
response: Timing typography is corrected; one enlarged quality view replaces the four-panel montage. The fault table now maps checks to codes. Matrix lookups validate explicit edges; no derivation engine or complete standards conformance is asserted. The archival DOI remains unavailable.
action: Revised figures, fault table, semantic boundary and archival package/checklist.

concern: Differentiate change types and explain large original sets.
response: The original component sets are retained. Change-aware scopes now contain 1–28 IDs across ten scenarios: an owner-only edit stays local, while classification, service and platform edits propagate under the declared policy. Scope size is not an accuracy score.
action: Added typed, two-hop and change-aware columns, exact policy checks and seed/dangling-ID caveats.

concern: Explain what oracle agreement demonstrates.
response: Agreement establishes implementation of the stated structural operation, not real-world causal impact or stakeholder usefulness. Both implementations share policy assumptions.
action: Correctness framing applied in abstract, methodology, results and conclusion; independent fixed-point reference added for revised policy.

concern: Present eight distinct checks rather than 240 independent trials.
response: Agreed. The eight fault checks repeat over 30 seed-generated topologies, with fixed mutation fixtures. Determinism means repetition does not create broader defect coverage.
action: Simplified results to exact-set agreement and a fault-code table; removed perfect-score emphasis.

concern: Compare Archi/coArchi and Structurizr.
response: Both are now explicitly represented. Git collaboration and model-as-code publication are established capabilities; comparison is documentation-based rather than a head-to-head benchmark.
action: Added capability table with primary-source documentation and no unsupported feature-absence claims.

concern: Report elapsed time and memory for the failed 100,000-object run.
response: The recovered original log gives approximately 10,760 s from benchmark-step start to cancellation. It contains no process RSS or phase telemetry; those missing observations cannot be reconstructed. The new re-attempt records elapsed time and process high-water RSS, including partial runs.
action: Preserved original log, documented unavailable historical memory, and added bounded supervisor, CSV checkpoints, phase JSONL and always-run artifact uploads.
status: Historical memory unavailable; new telemetry implemented

concern: Extend related work on AaC, MDE and recent GenAI.
response: The revision adds direct EA maintenance/continuous-delivery antecedents and a 2026 LLM-based EA-debt study. The distinction between probabilistic proposals and deterministic conformance checking is explicit.
action: Related Work, comparison and GenAI discussion revised; publisher/author records used for new references.

concern: Add a structured comparison across EA tools, IaC, AaC and GenAI.
response: The table covers representation/workflow, validation/review, domain, performance-evidence limits and AI role. Different tasks and datasets preclude a shared performance ranking.
action: Capability table includes Archi/coArchi, Structurizr, SAP LeanIX, Terraform, prior AaC/MDE, LLM EA analysis, and EA-Ops.

concern: Explain practical workflows and GenAI synergies.
response: An LLM can propose a patch and the existing gate can check explicit constraints, but a pass cannot validate source facts or strategic fitness. No LLM integration performance is claimed.
action: Integration and AI-Assisted Proposals subsection and adoption limitations added.

concern: Improve report performance and discuss typed impact.
response: Report counts are indexed, default reachability uses adjacency, and typed/depth-bounded/change-aware policies are implemented and checked. Total pipeline costs and heuristic impact limits remain explicit.
action: Implementation, tests, independent scenario checks and separate local scaling evidence supplied.

concern: Clarify hardware and archive implementation/data.
response: All original plots now mark the CPU transition and use medians consistently. Original artifacts and source/run provenance are preserved; the local revision environment is separate. Permanent DOI deposition remains necessary.
action: Rebuilt figures and provenance manifest; prepared release metadata, archival checklist and raw evidence.
